newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU presents Boeing with ultimatum on merger.
newsitem.headline: EU presents Boeing with ultimatum on merger.

text.p: Boeing Co. had until Monday night to make serious concessions over its proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp. or the European Commission could block the deal, European Union sources said.
"They (Boeing) know the risk they take if they do not come up with proper remedies by midnight," the source said.

The $14 billion merger between the two U.S. aircraft manufacturers has come under attack by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, who argues that it will increase Boeing's dominance of the world aircraft market due to McDonnell's strong customer base.
Van Miert also has sharply criticised Boeing's exclusive supply pacts with three major airlines -- AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Delta Air Lines.

Both sides said progress was made during talks over the weekend, but EU sources said they still did not overcome the Commission's concerns that Boeing would strengthen its dominant position in the market for airliners with more than 100 seats.
"Some progress has been made on one of the issues," the source said. But he added: "Altogether more progress needs to be made, to put it mildly -- hopefully before tonight sometime."
Although the Commission has until July 31 to rule on the deal, it must allow for time to consult national antitrust experts and to comply with other procedural rules.
In practice, it must make a final decision at its weekly meeting on July 23.

James Frank, Boeing's European executive vice president for government and public affairs, was hopeful a deal would be struck. "We still are optimistic that we will find a mutually acceptable solution," he said.
The merger was cleared by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission earlier this month without conditions.

But this did not change Van Miert's stance, the sources warned, recalling that the Commission may prohibit the merger if it is found to harm competition in the 15-nation bloc and fine Boeing if it goes ahead anyway.
The EU's advisory committee on mergers and acquisitions on July 4 unanimously backed Van Miert's opinion that the deal should not be allowed in its current form.

Some lawyers and industry representatives speculate the last-ditch talks focus on the controversial long-term exclusive supply pacts and the risk that defence contract money may be used to finance civil aviation projects.

Boeing is also expected to address the Commission's concern that it may tie the servicing and repair of McDonnell planes, which still account for a high share in some European fleets, to the acquisition of its own aircraft.
McDonnell's stock gained $1.375 to $73.0625 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Boeing added $1.1875 to $57.625, also on the NYSE.
